intent: Float a button over one edge of the transcript that appears while more content lies past that edge and scrolls there when pressed.
typical_uses: A jump-to-latest button at the bottom of a transcript the reader has scrolled back in
A jump-to-start button at the top of a long transcript

dont_use_when.situation: A jump to one particular message, or a scroll action outside the transcript frame

invariants.text: The button is active only while more content lies past the edge its `direction` names; the end button stays inactive while the scroller follows the end. Inactive, it carries `data-active="false"`, `inert` and `tabIndex={-1}`, ignores clicks, and message-scroller.module.css fades it out and slides it off that edge.
A click on the active button runs the consumer's `onClick` first; unless that calls `preventDefault`, the button blurs itself and scrolls to its edge with the given `behavior`.

Without `aria-label` the button is named "Scroll to end" or "Scroll to start" after its `direction`, even when children give it a visible label; without children it renders icon-only, a downward arrow the stylesheet turns upward for `direction="start"`, and children become a visible label beside the arrow.
By default the button renders the kit Button with `variant` and `size`; a `render` element replaces that Button entirely, so `variant` and `size` then have no effect and the arrow icon is gone.

message-scroller.module.css positions the button absolutely, centred horizontally in a left-to-right layout (in right-to-left the `inset-inline-start: 50%` plus physical `translate: -50%` pair leaves it a full button width off centre), near the bottom of the nearest positioned ancestor for `direction="end"` and near its top for `direction="start"`; that ancestor is MessageScroller when the button is its direct child.

anti_patterns.dont: Render the button only when useMessageScrollerScrollable reports the edge scrollable
anti_patterns.do_instead: Render it unconditionally - it activates and hides itself, and conditional mounting skips its fade

a11y.by: message-scroller.test.tsx finds the button with getByRole('button', { name: 'Scroll to end' }) and with the 'Back to top' aria-label override; the primitive's Button sets inert and tabIndex -1 while inactive

rtl.by: message-scroller.module.css `.button` pairs the logical `inset-inline-start: 50%` with the physical `translate: -50% 0`, so in a right-to-left layout the button is shifted away from the centre instead of onto it

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: The primitive's render prop takes an element or a function of the button's own state (`active`, `direction`), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. Given, it replaces the kit Button this component renders by default.

bad.title: Styling expected from variant on a custom render target
bad.why: `render` replaces the kit Button, so `variant` reaches nothing; style the rendered element itself or drop `render`.

render.description: TS: RenderProp<MessageScrollerButtonRenderState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. The primitive's render prop takes an element or a function of the button's own state (`active`, `direction`), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. Given, it replaces the kit Button this component renders by default.
